classification.difficultyReason: Read and total histogram frequencies, then divide the two-wicket frequency by the total.

inlines.text: The graph shows the frequency of wickets taken in a match of cricket.
What is the relative frequency of bowling 2 wickets in a match?

spec.description: Seven touching equal-width bars centred on wicket counts 0 through 6. Positive-axis arrowheads, half-unit rectangular grid, vertical ticks 0 through 9 and horizontal ticks 0 through 6. Equal-height final bars retain their dividing edge.
spec.mathematics: Frequencies for wickets 0,1,2,3,4,5,6 are respectively 5,9,7,4,3,1,1; total 30.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph data are supplied student givens. The answer 7/30 is excluded from the graph.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Total trials} &= 5+9+7+4+3+1+1 \\ \text{Total trials} &= 30 \\ \text{Relative frequency} &= \frac{\text{Frequency of 2 wickets}}{\text{Total trials}} \\ \text{Relative frequency} &= \frac{7}{30}\end{align*}$$
